question_text: According to the course material, types of business means the distinct business activity one can enter with the aim of satisfying customers, while kind of business is:
option_a: how to organize a business concern in order to carry out any of the types of business
option_b: the same as a GST course code
option_c: only the colour of the shop
explanation: Type = distinct activity (producer, processor, etc.). Kind = how the concern is organized (sole trader, partnership, company).

question_text: According to the course material, a producer is involved in producing goods that can be referred to as raw materials, gathering products in their original forms from natural resources such as:
explanation: Producers (farmer, mining, fishing, forestry) gather products in original forms from land and water.

question_text: According to the course material, businesses that change products from their original forms into more finished forms are:
explanation: Processors add value: paper mills, oil refineries, steel, yam into elubo, cassava into garri.

question_text: According to the course material, manufacturers turn raw or processed goods into finished goods ready for the market, and may combine the activities of producers and processors, as in the Dangote sugar example of farm, granulated sugar and:
explanation: Dangote as farmer is a producer; granulated sugar is processing; cubed packaged sugar makes him a manufacturer.

question_text: According to the course material, factors a businessman cannot control are called external or macro factors; the example given is that if Sharia does not allow selling alcohol in a state, in Niger State alcohol can only be sold in:
explanation: Macro/external factors cannot easily be changed. Example: alcohol in Niger State limited to barracks.

question_text: According to the course material, macro environment factors include demography, economy, social and cultural factors, political and legal forces, technology and:
explanation: Macro: demography, economy, social/cultural, political/legal, technology, competition.

question_text: According to the course material, micro or controllable factors include employees, managers, owner, financial institution, suppliers, consumers, government agencies, competitors and:
option_b: the climate of another continent only
explanation: Micro/controllable: employees, managers, owner, financial institutions, suppliers, consumers, government agencies, competitors, the public.

question_text: According to the course material, the purchasing power of a consumer depends on income, prices, savings and credit; real income per capital is affected by inflation, high unemployment and:
explanation: Real income per capita is affected by inflation, high unemployment and increased taxes, which reduce money people have to spend.

question_text: According to the course material, the specific or internal/micro environment includes employees, managers, owners, financial institutions, suppliers, customers, government agencies, competitors and:
explanation: Specific environment is what a businessman can face head on as directly related to his business.

question_text: According to the course material, employees can make a business fail or succeed; pay and conditions of employees covered by trade unions are dealt with through:
explanation: Pay and conditions of union-covered employees are dealt with through collective bargaining; managers more often bargain individually.

question_text: According to the course material, managers are the decision makers in an organization; they embody its attributes and philosophy and the success of the organization is usually bound up with:
explanation: Managers play a central role; organisational success is usually bound up with their personal performances.

question_text: According to Kurfi (2005), cited in the course material, a contract of sale is a contract whereby the seller transfers or agrees to transfer the property to the buyer for money consideration called:
explanation: Kurfi: seller transfers or agrees to transfer the property to the buyer for money consideration called price.

question_text: According to the course material, when you transfer the title of the goods to a buyer the contract is called sales; where possession is to pass on a future date with conditions attached it is called:
explanation: Transfer of title now = sales. Future transfer with conditions = agreement to sell; when conditions are fulfilled, sale has taken place.

question_text: According to the course material, contract of sale is distinguished from bailment, hire purchase and:
explanation: Sale is distinguished from bailment, hire purchase and exchange.

question_text: According to the course material, a condition is a term that if not fulfilled can cancel a contract, whereas a warranty if discovered leads to:
option_a: a right of damage only or possible replacement
option_b: automatic cancellation of the whole contract always
option_d: unlimited personal liability of every partner
explanation: Condition: breach can cancel the contract. Warranty: right of damages or possible replacement.

question_text: According to the course material, in a commercial contract time of delivery is necessary especially where perishable items are involved; if the time stipulated is breached:
option_a: the contract is affected as a stipulation as to time
explanation: Stipulation as to time: especially for perishables, breach of the stipulated time affects the contract.

question_text: According to Kurfi (2005), cited in the course material, a contract is a promise or set of promises for the breach of which the law gives a remedy, or the performance of which the law recognizes as a duty; contracts are classified into contract under seal and:
option_b: only insurance of oil and gas
explanation: Contract under seal is written, signed and sealed. Simple contract is informal: written, oral or mere conduct.

question_text: According to Kurfi (2005), cited in the course material, an expressed contract is when the parties manifest their agreement by words, while an implied contract is implied by:
option_a: the act or conducts of the parties and sanctioned by the law
explanation: Expressed: agreement by words (written, oral or under seal). Implied: by act or conduct, sanctioned by law.

question_text: According to the course material, a quasi-contract is illustrated by a doctor who treats an accident patient brought in by a passerby: the doctor will recover his cost of services from the patient, to discourage one party from:
option_a: unjustly benefiting from a contract that was not expressed
explanation: Quasi-contract resembles contract so one party does not unjustly benefit; the patient must pay the doctor.

question_text: According to the course material, a unilateral contract example is: if you find my lost GSM handset I will give you five hundred Naira; if found, you are bound to give the finder:
explanation: Unilateral: offer made, acceptance subject to legal obligation. Finder of the handset is entitled to N500.

question_text: According to the course material, essential elements of contract include offer, acceptance, consideration, intention to create legal relation, legal capacity of the parties, formalities required by the law, and:
option_a: legality of the object of the contract
option_b: the colour of the shop sign
explanation: Essential elements: offer, acceptance, consideration, intention to create legal relations, capacity, formalities, legality of object.

question_text: According to the course material, hire purchase is an agreement for the second party to have an item under some conditions; until such conditions are fulfilled the item is still that of:
option_b: the finder of a GSM handset
explanation: In hire purchase the item remains the first party's until the conditions are fulfilled.

question_text: According to the course material, bailment is an agreement that goods should be delivered to another party or transferred to a third party based on the instruction given by:
option_b: only the customer of a refinery
explanation: Bailment: goods delivered or transferred on the first party's instruction.

question_text: According to the course material, bad managers can cause a company to go under, frequent strikes and:
option_a: low salaries among related side effects
explanation: Side effects of bad managers: company can go under, frequent strikes, low salaries.

question_text: According to the course material, as economic conditions improve, incomes will rise and people will demand higher quality products and better service and they will be:
option_c: forced to buy only vacuum tubes
explanation: When conditions improve, people demand higher quality and better service and are willing to pay.
